name: Rooted Factors and Frozen Missing-Cube Witnesses Survive Block Replacement
statement: If $(A,0)$ is a rooted factor for the cut-vertex obstruction theorem and an active coordinate $z$ is replaced by a nonempty block $E$, then the constant lift of $0$ makes $W_E(A)$ a rooted factor. Suppose additionally that $0^{\{z\}}\in A$ and that each nonroot $x\in A$ has a missing-cube witness $J_x$ whose single-direction neighbours lie in $A$ and whose opposite word lies outside a fixed $C\supseteq A$. Then every nonroot lift in $W_E(A)$ has such a witness missing from $W_E(C)$. In particular, if $0$ is the unique corner of $A$, its constant lift is the unique corner of $W_E(A)$.
proof: Block-relative transfer preserves ordinary root attainability and root failure. Root-preserving old-coordinate minors commute with replacement; a new-coordinate contraction is a product and a new-coordinate root restriction is a peripheral expansion of proper rooted minors, so rooted minimality persists. For a lift $v=(y,t)$ choose an old nonroot preimage $x=(y,s)$, using $0^{\{z\}}$ for a nonconstant root fibre. Replace the old witness by its old directions outside $z$ together with block coordinates that move $t$ toward the constant pole opposite the missing trace. Every required neighbour is present in $W_E(A)$, while the opposite vertex is the constant lift of $x^{J_x}\notin C$. Applying this with $C=A$ protects every nonroot lift; the lifted old root cube certifies the remaining root corner.
